Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

grant verb

give what is asked

also grant a request, grant a wish, grant a favour, grant permission, I grant you

classical

Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7: nōn enim concēdō tibi plūs ut illum amēs quam ipse amō
Plaut. Cas. 2.3.47 (old numbering): illum mihi aequius est quam mē illī quae volō concēdere (Lewis & Short)

concēdō, concēdere, concessī, concessum

verb, third conjugation: aliquid alicui concēdere

grant, allow, yield (what is asked)

To grant something to someone, as a favour or from regard for them; in argument, to grant a point (concēdō, I grant that, with an accusative and infinitive). Its first sense is to go away, make way: Concēde hūc, move over here (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • veniam dare — grant a favour; give leave

    verb phrase: dō, dare, dedī, datum, with the dative of the person · also used · classical · Verg. A. 4.435–436: extrēmam hanc ōrō veniam … quam mihi cum dederit; Lewis & Short s.v. venia: “most usual in the phrase veniam dare, to grant a favor”

    Venia is indulgence, a favour; to ask one, veniam ōrāre, petere. It is also pardon: veniam dare can mean to forgive (see allow, give).

Examples

  • nōn enim concēdō tibi plūs ut illum amēs quam ipse amō

    for I don’t grant that you love him more than I doCic. Q. fr. 3.1.7

  • extrēmam hanc ōrō veniam (miserēre sorōris), quam mihi cum dederit cumulātam morte remittam

    this last favour I beg (pity your sister): when he has granted it, I shall repay it in full with my deathVerg. A. 4.435–436

See also allow, give, assume, even if, grant.

SourcesLewis & Short: concedo · Lewis & Short: venia

Quotation from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there. Vergil checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (11 November 2026); that edition reads dederit in 436, where others read dederis.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
